card.text: M30 is a globular star cluster in the Milky Way, about 8,460 parsecs away.

sources.label: Baumgardt & Vasiliev (2021), Accurate distances to Galactic globular clusters through a combination of Gaia EDR3, HST and literature data, MNRAS 505, 5957; Baumgardt's orbits table, NGC_7099: Rsun 8.46 ± 0.09 kpc
Wikipedia, "Messier 30"
sources.quote: Messier 30 is a globular cluster of stars in the southeast of the southern constellation of Capricornus, at about the declination of the Sun when the latter is at December solstice.

introduction.text: M30 is drawn as 919 of its member stars, measured by Gaia; each dot sits at its sky position, at the cluster's distance.

sources.label: Wikipedia, "Messier 30"
sources.quote: It was discovered by the French astronomer Charles Messier in 1764, who described it as a circular nebula without a star.

members.summary: One dot per member star inside the tidal radius, in its Gaia color. Its depth in the cluster is assumed, not measured.
